runtime_boundary: Represents the self-hosted gateway and the backends it manages, not the individual inference engines it can load and not any hosted service.
model_management: Models are installed from a built-in gallery through the web interface or the command-line tool, and backends are downloaded automatically to match detected hardware.
hardware_requirements: Dedicated container images cover CPU-only operation alongside NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Vulkan acceleration. The project documents automatic detection of available GPU capability and states that a GPU is not required.
operational_controls: A built-in web interface manages installations and configuration. A distributed mode registers GPU worker nodes with a front-end coordinator for scaling beyond one host.
strengths: Presents OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Messages, and Open Responses APIs over one self-hosted endpoint, spanning text, embeddings, images, and audio.
A model gallery plus automatic backend selection removes most manual setup for mixed hardware.
Documents container, orchestrated, and distributed multi-node deployment paths.
tradeoffs: Capability depends on which backend serves a given model, so behaviour is not uniform across the catalogue.
As a gateway it inherits the limits of the engines it loads rather than optimising execution itself.
Published operational visibility is centred on the web interface rather than a documented metrics surface.
license_note: The repository publishes a single MIT license file covering the gateway.
